entries.proposition: ALLELE CLASS / ZYGOSITY: one WWOX case, a missense plus a canonical splice-donor variant, labelled AR compound heterozygous; transcript NM_016373.4; WGS. Phase and parental genotypes are not reported.
entries.snippet: WWOX (NM_016373.4) c.911C>A (p.Ser304Tyr) c.230+1G>T (Splice donor) AR, compound heterozygous

entries.proposition: PHENOTYPE BAND: focal seizures from one month, psychomotor delay and spastic ataxia; imaging with hydrocephalus and atrophy; an affected sibling with epilepsy and spastic ataxia died at 11 months (sibling not genotyped in the paper).
entries.snippet: Focal 1 PMD, spastic ataxia Spike-slow wave complexes in the right parietotemporal leads
entries.anchor: Table 1, WWOX row, phenotype and EEG columns

entries.proposition: AFFECTED SIBLING, reported in the table, not genotyped in the paper.
entries.snippet: with epilepsy and spastic ataxia, died at the age of 11 months

entries.proposition: BOTH VARIANTS REPORTED AS NOVEL by the authors; the pathogenicity call is the paper's own (ACMG on the Franklin platform), with no per-variant class printed.
entries.snippet: This patient was found to have compound heterozygous variants in the WWOX gene. Both genetic variants have not previously been described.
entries.anchor: Results, paragraph on the WWOX case

entries.proposition: HOW THE CALL WAS MADE: ACMG/AMP five-tier classification on a commercial interpretation platform.
entries.snippet: Variant interpretation followed the 5-level classification system recommended by the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics and the Association for Molecular Pathology (ACMG/AMP) and was conducted on the Franklin platform (Franklin by Genoox, Genoox, USA).
entries.anchor: Materials and Methods, 'Interpretation of Genetic Variants'

entries.proposition: INCLUSION CRITERION THE WWOX CASE DOES NOT OBVIOUSLY MEET: no structural MRI change, while the WWOX case's MRI shows hydrocephalus and atrophy.
entries.snippet: The absence of structural changes in magnetic resonance imaging of the brain (MRI), which may be the cause of epilepsy
